meta.title: Suffrage and social-protection adoption by country

coverage.scope: 61 current and historical country/polity rows, prioritising states in the UN 1953 comparative franchise memorandum and major countries. This is a first evidence-backed calibration cohort, not a complete global census.

definitions.male_suffrage_year: First broad/universal male national franchise milestone only when a comparative source gives a defensible year. Null means not independently verified in this package; it does not mean no male suffrage.
definitions.female_suffrage_year: First national franchise grant to women, including restricted grants where explicitly noted. It is not necessarily the year of the first actual election.
definitions.female_suffrage_full_equal_year: Year equal national voting terms are documented where the initial grant was restricted; null means the first grant was already equal or the reviewed sources did not establish a later equalisation date.
definitions.social_insurance_year: Earliest of the five national statutory branches in the ILO 2019 comparison: work accident, health, pension, unemployment, family support. The table is selected OECD coverage, not a global first-ever database.
definitions.old_age_pension_year: ILO table's first pension-insurance legislation year; not necessarily the first means-tested pension, first occupational pension or universal non-contributory pension.
definitions.unemployment_insurance_year: ILO table's first unemployment-insurance legislation year; may be voluntary subsidised, compulsory, or implemented later than enactment. Type is specified when known.
definitions.suspended: Periods when competitive constitutional national elections or ordinary parliamentary democracy were suspended/restricted. These do not automatically mean the legal right to vote was repealed.

qualityLegend.verified: Primary law/official chronology or UN/IPU country record directly confirms the year.
qualityLegend.supported: Credible comparative study or official historical synthesis supports the year; interpretive scope is documented.
qualityLegend.partial: Country included, but one or more requested historical dates remain unverified and are null.

meta.dateConvention: Years only; dates are legal grant or legislation year, not first election year, unless note says otherwise.
meta.caution: Do not infer political openness from suffrage law alone. Formal eligibility, effective access, election competitiveness, race/property/education restrictions, gender equality and regime interruption are separate dimensions.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General, A/2462: Franchise of women (26 August 1953)
sources.note: Tables I–VII distinguish national from local franchise, restricted grants and equal rights; especially pp. 10–18.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service, Statistics on Women in National Governments Around the Globe (R45483)
sources.type: US Congressional Research Service synthesis using IPU
sources.note: Cross-checks women’s national voting rights and records staged restrictions; e.g. US racial disenfranchisement and Canada Indigenous exclusions.

sources.title: IPU Parline data dictionary: women’s right to vote
sources.note: Defines right-to-vote year, national/local scope, restricted/unrestricted status and restriction notes.

sources.title: Our World in Data: Men’s universal right to vote (Lexical Index 2026)
sources.note: LIED v6.9, 1789–2025; binary universal male national suffrage, ignores informal barriers and some exclusions; values should be extracted for automated year detection before production calibration.

sources.title: Our World in Data: Universal right to vote (Lexical Index 2026)
sources.note: LIED v6.9 country-year indicator; distinguish formal universal suffrage from effective competitive elections.

sources.title: V-Dem Codebook v16 (2026)
sources.note: Defines legal de jure suffrage indicators and distinguishes them from de facto enfranchisement when electoral regimes are interrupted.

sources.title: Pilon, Electoral transformation in Western Europe in the 19th and early 20th century: an overview
sources.note: Comparative table of full male suffrage dates including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada (range), Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, UK and USA.

sources.title: Electoral transformation in Western Europe in the 19th and early 20th century
sources.note: Table 3 gives universal male suffrage milestones in Western Europe; distinguishes women’s suffrage introduced together with male franchise.

sources.title: Global Struggle for Suffrage Expansion: The European Case for Male Suffrage in the Nineteenth Century
sources.note: Provides male franchise reform years for Greece, Spain, Argentina, Uruguay and selected European countries.

sources.title: ILO, Global social security and economic development: Retrospect and prospect (2019)
sources.note: Table 1, printed p.18, adapted from Schmidt 2005, reports first legislation years for work accidents, health insurance, pension insurance, unemployment insurance and family support in 23 selected OECD countries. Column order verified from page image.

sources.title: ILO, Whither Social Security? Annex 6: Unemployment – date of first law
sources.note: Lists first unemployment-branch laws by region; distinguishes broad national dates and notes Republic of Korea implementation in 1995.

sources.title: US Social Security Administration archive: Social Security in America, unemployment compensation
sources.note: Contemporaneous 1930s tables of compulsory and subsidized voluntary unemployment-insurance legislation, dates and coverage.

sources.title: US Social Security Administration: historical development of social insurance
sources.note: Explains German Bismarckian social insurance, Danish 1891 old-age pension, British 1908 pension and 1911 insurance reforms.

sources.title: The Political Origin of Pension Funding, Table 1: Development of Pension Systems
sources.note: Distinguishes first pension program from first major broad-coverage program; first programs may cover only occupational or selected groups.

sources.title: ISSA Country Profiles – methodology and coverage
sources.note: Current statutory scheme descriptions for 190+ countries; use to validate present-day scheme structures, not to infer historical start dates.
